name: sup-run-fallback-unknown
notes: `vdelta run`'s 2-stage default baseline resolution (issue #72): when stage 1 (`previous-comparable`) abstains `baseline-missing` and stage 2 (`previous-superset`) abstains for a *different* reason, stage 2's report is what's returned, so the more specific reason surfaces to the consumer instead of being collapsed into `baseline-missing`. `C`'s only series-mate `A` (selector `['src']`) and `C` (selector `['src/a', 'tests']`) neither contain one another: `'src'` overlaps `'src/a'` without covering `'tests'`, so `selectorRelation` returns `'unknown'` (same shape as `sup-abstain-relation-unknown`). `A` is never a candidate, but the undecided relation is recorded, so stage 2 abstains `selector-relation-unknown`/`determined` -- distinct from `baseline-missing` -- and that stage-2 report (with `baseline: null` and no `near_miss`, since `previous-superset` reports never carry that `previous-comparable`-only field) is what `vdelta run` returns.
